description: System-level power controls. lock sends the ⌃⌘Q lock shortcut through System Events, which needs Accessibility and Automation > System Events. When either permission is denied, lock starts the screen saver instead, which locks the session only when "Require password after screen saver begins or display is turned off" is set to Immediately in System Settings > Lock Screen; the method field reports which one ran. sleep_display turns off all displays immediately. Both are reversed by any input (wake or unlock).

action.description: lock — lock the screen with the ⌃⌘Q shortcut, or start the screen saver when the shortcut is denied; method in the result says which. sleep_display — turn off all displays.

name: macos_control_system

error.description: Present when the call failed. Absent on success.

code.description: JSON-RPC error code for this failure.

reason.description: Machine-readable failure mode. Declared by this tool: `accessibility_required`: lock: the ⌃⌘Q shortcut was denied Accessibility or Automation > System Events, and the ScreenSaverEngine fallback could not start. Other values are possible when a failure originates below the handler.

recovery.description: Actionable next step for the caller.

message.description: Human-readable description of what went wrong.

method.description: How lock ran; present for action=lock only. keystroke — the ⌃⌘Q shortcut was sent, which locks the session. screen_saver — the shortcut was denied and the screen saver was started, which locks the session only when "Require password after screen saver begins or display is turned off" is set to Immediately.

title: Control macOS System
